**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**Copy to:** Darlene, Supervisor; Transportation Office  
**From:** [Your Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9  
**Date:** [Date Submitted]  
**Subject:** Written Statement Regarding Amara’s Afternoon Transportation on October 27, 2026

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am submitting this statement in response to your complaint dated October 29, which my supervisor, Darlene, provided to me on November 3. I understand that this statement will be placed in my file and that you will receive a copy. I want to explain what happened during the afternoon route on Tuesday, October 27, why I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary, and what I observed at the time.

First, I understand that not finding your child where you expected her to be would be frightening. I have grandchildren, and I can appreciate how upsetting that situation would be. I am sorry for the worry and difficult afternoon you experienced. At the same time, I want to be clear that my decision to keep Amara on the bus and return her to school was made to follow the district’s procedure for her safe release.

On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara, a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary, was riding the bus and had the green tag on her bag indicating that an adult must be present at her stop before she can be released.

The scheduled time for the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street is 3:50 p.m. I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. and remained there until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult at the corner who was there to receive Amara. Because she is a kindergarten student requiring an adult at the stop, I did not allow her to leave the bus.

My understanding of the district’s rule for kindergarten riders is that when an adult is not present at the stop, the student must remain on the bus and be returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. That is the procedure I followed. I could not release Amara without seeing the adult who was there to meet her.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch to report the situation. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 other children remaining on the bus. I continued the route before returning Amara to Fairmont Elementary.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you or see you waving. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I cannot say whether it blocked my view of you, but I include it here as part of the conditions I observed. I am not saying that you were not there. I am saying that I did not see you and therefore could not confirm that an adult was present to receive Amara.

I also want to address the concern that I did not respond to you. I did not knowingly ignore you or refuse to acknowledge you. Had I seen you waving, I would have been able to respond to what I saw. From my position on the bus, however, I did not see an adult waiting for Amara.

With other children still aboard, I could not leave the bus unattended to walk across the road or look for someone in a parked vehicle. My responsibility was to maintain supervision of the students on the bus while following the procedure for a child whose receiving adult was not visible at the stop. Keeping Amara aboard was the safe action available to me under those circumstances.

Your complaint also states that I drove away laughing. I was not laughing. As we were pulling away, I was directing the fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I was addressing a student safety issue, not making light of Amara’s situation or your concerns.

During the remainder of the trip, Amara appeared calm. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were going on a little extra trip. I mention this to describe what I observed while she was in my care, not to minimize the worry you experienced.

We arrived back at Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked Amara into the school office and turned her over to Mrs. Petrakis. I did not leave her outside or send her into the building alone.

I respectfully request that the Transportation Office promptly preserve and review the available camera footage from Bus 41 for the October 27 afternoon run. The review should include our arrival and wait at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, our departure, and any available recording relevant to the concerns raised in the complaint. I would like the footage considered alongside this statement so that the review is based on the available evidence as well as each person’s account.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years without a write-up. I take that record seriously because it reflects the responsibility I feel toward the children entrusted to me. I include it as background, while recognizing that this incident should be reviewed on its own facts. My decision that afternoon was based on Amara’s green-tag requirement, the absence of an adult I could see, and the district’s return-to-school procedure.

Going forward, it would help me identify you if you could wait on the bus side of the street, in a safe location consistent with the school’s directions, or step out of your parked vehicle where I can clearly see you. I would welcome the Transportation Office’s help in confirming a safe, clear arrangement so that we both know what to expect at dismissal.

I am glad to continue driving Amara and want our daily contact to be comfortable and respectful. My purpose in providing this statement is not to argue with you, but to explain my actions accurately and help prevent another upsetting afternoon. We share the same concern: making sure Amara gets home safely and is released to the adult there to meet her.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]  
School Bus Driver  
Bus 41, Route 9
